core_obligations: Prepare the extensions: choose B_j contained in C_j as in the preparation lemma for the given a and b, and use the glueing lemma for maximal ideals to produce one finite extension B contained in C with C_j isomorphic to C_{m_j} for every j; let m_{j,k} be the maximal ideals of C lying over m_j (proof lines 967-972).

Write both sides in local terms: the local factorisations a = u_{j,k} pi_{j,k}^{f_{j,k}} and b = v_{j,k} pi_{j,k}^{g_{j,k}} hold by the choice of C, and substituting them into the definitions gives the displayed expression for the tame symbol of A as a product over the pairs (j, k) and the displayed expression for each tame symbol of B_j as a product over k, both featuring the same residue classes (proof lines 973-993).

Conclude by transitivity of norms: the two displays differ only in that the double product over pairs (j, k) is regrouped as the product over j of a norm for kappa(m_{j,k})/kappa(m_j), and the norm tower lemma says exactly that this regrouping is legitimate, yielding the asserted identity (proof lines 994-996).
proof_roadmap: Use the preparation lemma inside each B_j and then the glueing lemma to assemble a single finite extension B contained in C whose localisations are the prepared local extensions (proof lines 967-972).
Write out the local factorisations of a and b in C and substitute them into the definition of both sides, obtaining two explicit products of norm terms (proof lines 973-993).
Identify the two products using transitivity of the norm in the tower kappa(m_{j,k})/kappa(m_j)/kappa(m) (proof lines 994-996).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the tame symbol of a pair of nonzerodivisors on a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring as the product of the norms of the tame symbols computed in the finite local extensions B_j, under the hypothesis that the maximal ideal is not an associated prime of B and that B/A is killed by a power of it (statement lines 953-963). The proof first has to make both sides computable: a preparation lemma supplies local extensions C_j in which a and b factor as units times powers of local parameters, and the glueing lemma for maximal ideals assembles them into one finite extension B contained in C, after which both the symbol on A and the symbols on the B_j are written as explicit double and single products of norm terms (proof lines 967-993). The two expressions are then identified by regrouping the product, which is exactly transitivity of the norm in a tower of residue field extensions. The claim is H2: a two-step preparation followed by a norm bookkeeping identity.
